system: Tibetan Rabjung (rab byung) 60-year cycle - element x animal x gender

epoch_rule.note: Year 1 of Rabjung cycle 1 = 1027 CE = FIRE-FEMALE-HARE. This is the pivotal fix: the commonly transcribed 'starts Wood-Male-Tiger' belongs to the Chinese sexagenary (mekhor) convention, not the Rabjung count. Laufer (1911) confirms Tibetan chronologies designate the first year of the first cycle 'fire-hare' and fixes 1027 (not Csoma's 1026) as epoch.

formula.rabjung_numbering: cycle m = (Y-1027)//60 + 1 ; year-in-cycle n = ((Y-1027) mod 60) + 1 ; year 1 of every cycle = Fire-Female-Hare
formula.janson_reference_formulas: Y = 60m + n + 966 ; n = (Y - 1026) amod 60 (Svante Janson, arXiv:1401.6285 eq 4.1-4.2)

losar_note: A Rabjung year label attaches to the Tibetan year that BEGINS at Losar (Feb 4 - Mar 5 window in the 20th c., drifting later; Phugpa calendar). Gregorian dates before Losar belong to the PREVIOUS element/animal/gender label. Exact mapping needs a Losar date table (e.g., Janson Table 1 / almanac); without it, degrade Jan-mid-Feb lookups to approximate/unavailable per spec 18 degradation rule.
